summary: S. 761 establishes the Truth and Healing Commission on Indian Boarding School Policies in the United States within the legislative branch. The commission is tasked with investigating the historical and ongoing impacts of federal Indian Boarding School policies, which involved removing American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian children from their homes. The bill also sets up advisory committees, subcommittees, burial management rules, and requires periodic reports and recommendations.

affected_groups.effect: Will have opportunities to provide testimony at regional convenings, receive trauma-informed care support, participate in investigative and healing processes, and benefit from repatriation, record-sharing, and burial management provisions.
affected_groups.group: Native Americans (American Indians, Alaska Natives, and Native Hawaiians), including survivors, descendants, and tribal

affected_groups.effect: Required to cooperate with information requests, assist advisory committees, and respond to the commission's final report recommendations.

key_provisions: Establishes the Truth and Healing Commission on Indian Boarding School Policies in the United States within the legislative branch along with a Survivors Truth and Healing Subcommittee, a Native American Truth and Healing Advisory Committee, and a Federal and Religious Truth and Healing Advisory Committee.
Requires the commission to conduct a comprehensive interdisciplinary investigation into the social, cultural, economic, emotional, and physical effects of Indian Boarding School policies.

Directs the commission and advisory bodies to locate and identify marked and unmarked burial sites and records associated with Indian boarding schools, and to share burial locations and identities with affected families and tribes.
Mandates that the commission hold public and private convenings across Bureau of Indian Affairs regions and in Hawaii, providing trauma-informed care services for participants.
Requires the commission to submit annual reports, an initial report within four years, and a final report detailing findings, conclusions, and recommendations.

Clarifies that the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act applies to cultural items related to Indian boarding schools, and allows federal agencies to enter into co-stewardship agreements for cemeteries and school sites.
Authorizes $90,000,000 from specified existing funding sources to carry out the act.

summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 761 establishes the Truth and Healing Commission on Indian Boarding School Policies in the United States within the legislative branch. The commission is tasked with investigating the historical and ongoing impacts of federal Indian Boarding School policies, which involved removing American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian children from their homes. The bill also sets up advisory committees, subcommittees, burial management rules, and requires periodic reports and recommendations.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a formal federal commission and structured advisory bodies dedicated to investigating, documenting, and addressing the long-term impacts of historical federal policies regarding Indian boarding schools, affecting federal record-keeping, historical research, tribal repatriation, and burial management.
